title: Keys, black-note playing and Triangle Jazz Blues printed in Chicago
summary: He and Bosdorfer played in hard black-note keys, and they work out the key of Triangle Jazz Blues, printed in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I could ask you some technical questions from what I can read of the music. Like on, where did the rags usually change key? Like in Triangle Jazz Blues, didn't it change after the third string or something? Do you remember?

No, I wasn't. Yeah. You see, I used to play all the way to black notes. We used to call it, Bosdorff was the same fellow. He played all on the black notes. We used to say he was a black note piano player. I was too. Yeah.
Playing in all those hard keys.
Yeah, I was wondering what key Joe Martinez wrote this thing of mine. Well. Because I know I played in... You know, One Sharp. Yeah. One Sharp. Ain't that F Sharp?
We got a better copy here.
Because that's how... I don't know whether he took it down. If he did, maybe that's why it was so difficult for people.
What's that? G Sharp? G Sharp?
I don't know, man. That's one thing.
And then it changes to two shops for the last thing.
Yeah. Yeah. But that was printed up in Chicago for this company.
They had... They'd send it off to Chicago to be printed. That's funny.
